title: Using a thimble
subtitle: How to wear and use a thimble to push the needle through dense fabric without pain.
excerpt: A thimble protects the tip of the middle finger when pushing the needle through fabric. Most beginners find them awkward at first but uncomfortable sessions without one are worse. This technique entry covers fitting, holding, and the moment to push.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776. Thimble use described in the preliminary equipment chapter.

glossaryTerms.definition: A protective cap worn on the middle finger of the stitching hand. The dimpled metal or leather surface catches the needle end and allows the stitcher to push the needle through fabric using the finger rather than the thumb and forefinger alone.

content.text: protects the fingertip from the sharp end of the needle eye when pushing it through cloth. On thin fabric it is optional. On canvas, heavy linen, or multiple layers, a session without one will leave the finger sore.
Fit the thimble on the middle finger of your stitching hand. It should slide on without force but stay in place when the hand is relaxed.
Check that the tip of the thimble extends about 3 mm beyond the fingertip. A thimble that covers the whole finger joint is too large; one that leaves the tip exposed is too small.
How to push with a thimble
Hold the needle between the thumb and forefinger as usual, with the eye end resting against the thimble tip.
As you push through thick fabric, apply the force through the thimble-tipped middle finger onto the eye end of the needle, rather than pinching the needle shaft hard.
Let the thimble's dimples catch the needle end so it doesn't slip.

items.symptom: The thimble feels clumsy and you keep removing it
items.cause: The thimble is the wrong size, or you are not yet used to pushing with the middle finger.
items.fix: Try one size smaller. Wear the thimble for short sessions even when not strictly needed; the habit builds quickly.

items.symptom: The needle slips off the thimble surface
items.cause: Smooth metal thimbles have fewer dimples and the needle slides off.
items.fix: Try a thimble with a ridged or heavily dimpled top, or a leather thimble with a metal insert at the tip.

content.text: A well-fitting thimble makes canvas work and goldwork more comfortable. The habit takes time to build. Once you have it, the thimble stops finger damage during heavy work and keeps sessions from ending early.
